epic:#27261#1 · marchtian · session_017ihL2c5z3q4h8inrn5kwqV
Claim amendment · 2026-10-30T01:41Z

The card thread stopped on a spec question, as the claim asks. On `main`, the type-compat matrix (`packages/spec/src/data/type-compat.ts`) knows no EDM names. It serves both draft suggestion (`suggestFieldTypeForSqlType`) and Gate 2 boot validation (`isCompatible`). So every `Edm.*` column canonicalises to `unknown`: drafts come out all `text`, and an object mapping `Edm.Int32` to `number` is a `type_mismatch` error at boot under `onMismatch: 'fail'`.

PM ruling: option A. The matrix gains an `odata` arm: `SqlDialect` adds `'odata'`, and `DIALECT_ALIASES.odata` maps the EDM primitives, with `Edm.Int64` and `Edm.Decimal` lossy as their SQL kin are. The service maps the driver's `odata-4.0` dialect onto it. This keeps one type table for draft, catalog and Gate 2. A second EDM table inside `service-datasource` (option B) was declined: it would leave the CLI and every other matrix reader EDM-blind.

- File surface adds `packages/spec/src/data/type-compat.ts`, its tests, and the generated references the change re-records.
- Clause-② becomes `yes`: a published union widens. The PR names every exhaustive consumer of `SqlDialect` in the repository, `ui/` included, and updates it in the same PR.
- Contract face: the PR body says "Fable review owed". It lands only after a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record PASS on its head.

Navigation lookups read the registry (no contract change). The draft's snake_case field names with `external.columnMap` for PascalCase EDM properties stay inside `service-datasource`.

epic:#27261#1 · marchtian · session_017ihL2c5z3q4h8inrn5kwqV
Claim amendment 2 · 2026-10-30T01:41Z

Second half of the option-A ruling (6512853588). `isCompatible` lists `lookup` only under the `uuid` row, so a lookup over a foreign-key column of type `Edm.Int32`, `int` or `varchar` is a Gate 2 `type_mismatch` today, for SQL federation too. The same file adds `lookup` and `master_detail` to the exact sets of the text, integer and bigint rows. Gate 2 gets looser and nothing that passes today fails. The changeset and PR say so in plain words for SQL federation.

A single-valued navigation becomes a lookup only when it has a `ReferentialConstraint` whose dependent property is on the entity type and whose referenced property is the target's single key. Every other navigation is left out and named in the review notes. No further surface change.
